definitions.gloss: floor plan; plan view; plan drawing
definitions.explanation: A drawing that shows a building, room, or site as seen from directly above — with walls, doors, furniture, or other features drawn flat on a two-dimensional plane. Used in architecture, real estate, and interior design.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}の{平面図|へいめんず}。
examples.english: The floor plan of a house.

examples.japanese: この{平面図|へいめんず}を{見|み}ると、{部屋|へや}の{配置|はいち}がよく{分|わ}かる。
examples.english: Looking at this floor plan, you can clearly see the layout of the rooms.

examples.japanese: {建築士|けんちくし}が{新|あたら}しいマンションの{平面図|へいめんず}を{描|か}いた。
examples.english: The architect drew up the floor plan for the new apartment building.

examples.japanese: {不動産|ふどうさん}のサイトでは、{物件|ぶっけん}ごとに{詳|くわ}しい{平面図|へいめんず}が{掲載|けいさい}されている。
examples.english: On real-estate websites, a detailed floor plan is posted for each property.

notes:
Composed of {平面|へいめん} (flat surface, plane) and {図|ず} (diagram, drawing). A {平面図|へいめんず} shows a structure or area from a bird's-eye (top-down) perspective, as if the roof has been removed. It is one of the standard types of architectural drawings, alongside {立面図|りつめんず} (elevation) and {断面図|だんめんず} (cross-section).

USAGE:
Frequently seen in real-estate listings, house-plan magazines, and building-construction documents. Also used in geometry classes when depicting flat figures.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平面図|へいめんず}を{描|か}く: to draw a floor plan
- {平面図|へいめんず}を{見|み}る: to look at a floor plan
- {平面図|へいめんず}に{示|しめ}す: to indicate on the floor plan
- {詳細|しょうさい}な{平面図|へいめんず}: a detailed floor plan

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {間取|まど}り: room layout — less technical; refers to the arrangement of rooms rather than the drawing itself
- {立面図|りつめんず}: elevation drawing — shows the exterior as seen from the front or side
- {断面図|だんめんず}: cross-section drawing — shows the interior as if sliced vertically
- {見取|みと}り{図|ず}: sketch map, rough layout drawing — a simpler, less precise version often drawn by hand
